transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-02-27
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 60 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Shea (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM), Janie Park (Acme - Lead ML Eng), Marcus Li (Acme - Infra), Sofia Gomez (Acme - PM)
---
Summary: quick run through POC goals, bench harness integration, load shape and streaming considerations; capture success criteria and timeline.
Topics: benchmark harness, streaming vs non-streaming, load testing, KV/prefix cache, data residency, SLOs, env access
---
Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we can start, I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account.
[00:10] Marcus Li: Hey Maya, thanks. Sorry a little late, connection just, yeah.
[00:15] Maya Chen: No worries. Liam, you want to intro yourself and what you'll cover?
[00:20] Liam O'Shea: Yeah hi, I'm Liam, I'll be the SE on the POC. Today I want to align on the benchmark plan, how your scripts plug into our harness, and talk streaming vs non-streaming tradeoffs.
[00:33] Janie Park: Great, I'm Janie, lead ML eng at Acme. We own the intent classification service. We want to validate latency at load and how quality holds up versus smaller models we also use.
[00:45] Sofia Gomez: And I'm Sofia, product, I'm mostly here for success criteria and timelines.
[00:50] Priya Nair: Hi all, Priya from CSM, will help coordinate next steps.
[00:55] Liam O'Shea: Quick agenda: 1) success metrics & SLOs, 2) workload sizing and traffic shape, 3) harness integration details (scripts, auth, streaming vs non), 4) schedule & next steps.
[01:10] Janie Park: Sounds good. Our high-level success criteria: p95 latency under 250ms for single-turn classification at 512 tokens, throughput ~200 qps sustained, and model quality no worse than our current baseline (we'll provide eval prompts).
[01:30] Marcus Li: On infra side we need to know VPC requirements, what ports, KMS for keys, and whether we need direct peering or can use temporary SSH tunnel.
[01:40] Maya Chen: Great. For VPC/private POC we usually request a one-time VPN or temporary VPC peering. We support customer-managed KMS/HSM. We'll put exact network checklist in the harness doc.
[01:55] Liam O'Shea: On the p95 and throughput, helpful to confirm your traffic shape. Is that steady 200 qps or spiky with bursts to 500?
[02:05] Janie Park: Mostly steady with diurnal spikes; during peak marketing campaigns we have bursts to 450 qps for a few minutes.
[02:15] Liam O'Shea: Ok we'll design the benchmark to include steady state and burst phases. For the harness integration, do you have existing k6 or locust scripts, or are they in-house python load drivers?
[02:27] Janie Park: We have a python driver that wraps requests and some async streaming tests, we can share. It's not fully parameterized though.
[02:34] Liam O'Shea: That's fine. Typical options: either we adapt your scripts to call Redwood's REST endpoint, or we provide our benchmark harness repo and you drop in the prompt set and a lightweight adapter. The latter is faster to reproduce on our side.
[02:48] Maya Chen: And for streaming vs non-streaming: if your client reads partial tokens we should test both. Streaming usually lowers perceived latency but can complicate p95 measurement because of first-byte vs end-to-end timings.
[03:02] Janie Park: We're mainly interested in end-to-end classification time, but our front end streams tokens to show progress. So both matter.
[03:12] Marcus Li: On the infra note, streaming also means long-lived connections — we need to confirm connection limits, proxies, etc.
[03:20] Liam O'Shea: Right. We'll include connection concurrency tests and socket churn. Also test both the streaming (SSE/websocket style) and non-streaming batch path. We'll instrument first-byte latency and full-response latency.
[03:35] Sofia Gomez: Ok on timelines — we're targeting an internal decision by end of March, so we need results in the first week of March ideally.
[03:44] Maya Chen: That's doable. Proposed timeline: this week share harness + network checklist, customer shares scripts and sample prompts by Mar 3, we run initial dry-run Mar 4-5, formal benchmark Mar 8-10, review and results by Mar 12. Does that align?
[03:59] Janie Park: Yes, aligns with our timeline.
[04:05] Liam O'Shea: Now some technical details on the harness: our harness supports two modes — streaming client mode and synchronous mode. It supports load shaping phases: ramp, steady, spike. It collects per-request timings, token counts, model variant used, and detailed logs. We'll need a small adapter that maps your request shape to our API, auth either API key or temporary mTLS token.
[04:25] Janie Park: We'll prefer mTLS for the private POC. We use customer KMS for signing keys.
[04:32] Maya Chen: Noted. We support mTLS and can also provide a temporary API gateway if that's simpler.
[04:38] Marcus Li: For KV cache/prefix caching — we have several repeated prefixes in our user intents. How do you recommend we test cache warmup and hit rates?
[04:48] Liam O'Shea: Good question — typical approach: 1) pre-warm with a set of common prefixes at low QPS, 2) run steady-state load and capture cache hit/miss metrics, 3) run an A/B with and without KV caching/with different cache sizes to measure tail latency impact. We'll provide scripts to control pre-warm and to emit cache metrics.
[05:05] Janie Park: There's sometimes a mismatch — our current pipeline uses a KV cache that sits in front of a smaller distilled model. We want to ensure Redwood's batching and cache don't regress quality.
[05:15] Liam O'Shea: We'll include quality checks — run your prompt eval set on both systems and compute micro-F1 and also sample outputs for manual review. We'll tie quality thresholds to pass/fail criteria in the benchmark.
[05:30] Sofia Gomez: On pass/fail how strict should the regression tolerance be? 1%? 3%?
[05:36] Maya Chen: Commonly customers pick 1-3% depending on business sensitivity. For classification, 1% can be tight; I'd suggest 2% as a starting point and we can adjust.
[05:45] Janie Park: Ok 2% seems reasonable to start.
[05:50] Liam O'Shea: About tooling — our harness will emit CSV/JSON reports and we'll share a dashboard link with per-request traces. If you want, we can also push traces to your internal tracing system via a webhook.
[06:02] Marcus Li: We use Datadog, sending via webhook is fine. We'll need some sample metrics names so our SREs can map them.
[06:10] Liam O'Shea: We'll send the metric mapping doc. 
[06:13] Janie Park: Quick note on prompt length: some of our classification prompts are 512 tokens, others are 128. Please ensure the harness varies prompt sizes to simulate real traffic.
[06:23] Liam O'Shea: We'll parameterize prompt length distribution. Can you share tokenization behavior for your inputs (e.g., avg token counts)?
[06:30] Janie Park: We'll export token histograms along with sample prompts.
[06:35] Maya Chen: On model variants — do you have preferred candidate models? We can recommend quantized variants for cost, or larger FP16 models for quality.
[06:45] Janie Park: We want a near-production model; currently using a 7B distilled model. We're open to trying a 13B quantized variant if cost looks ok.
[06:54] Liam O'Shea: We'll include both in the benchmark as model A/B and measure tokens-per-second, cost per 1M tokens, and latency. Also measure memory and GPU utilization.
[07:05] Sofia Gomez: Pricing visibility is key for us. We'll need estimated per-token costs for each config.
[07:12] Maya Chen: We'll include cost estimates and a cost/perf dashboard from Redwood Optimize for the run.
[07:18] Marcus Li: On security and compliance — we need SOC2 documentation, audit log retention, and the ability to rotate keys.
[07:27] Maya Chen: We have SOC2 and ISO docs in our security pack; we'll share those. Audit logs are available and we support key rotation via your KMS.
[07:36] Janie Park: For the harness, what's the expected impact of batching on tail latency? Our traffic has low variance but tail matters.
[07:45] Liam O'Shea: Batching improves throughput but can add latency at low QPS due to waiting to fill a batch. We'll run microbenchmarks at multiple batch sizes and measure p50/p95/p99. If your requirement is strict p95, we'll tune batch sizes and batching timeouts and test quantized kernels as well.
[08:02] Janie Park: Makes sense. Please capture per-request batch size in the logs so we can see when requests waited.
[08:09] Liam O'Shea: Yep. We'll log batch size, wait time, and K V cash hit/miss (sorry K V cash -> KV cache — transcriber sometimes does that).
[08:18] Maya Chen: (laughs) yep, KV cache.
[08:21] Marcus Li: For the private deployment, we need to know if offline inference (air-gapped) is supported for later phases.
[08:29] Maya Chen: We do support an on-prem package for air-gapped/regulated workloads; separate licensing. For POC we'll do private VPC deployment.
[08:36] Sofia Gomez: Any risk of model drift during the test — do you snapshot models and versions?
[08:42] Liam O'Shea: We always pin model versions for a POC and record model hashes so results are reproducible.
[08:48] Janie Park: Ok good. On instrumentation access — can we get read-only access to the Redwood dashboard for the run?
[08:55] Priya Nair: Yes we'll provision read-only accounts for your team and SREs.
[08:59] Maya Chen: A couple of practicals for harness integration: 1) auth (mTLS or API key), 2) endpoint and model name, 3) prompt adapter example (we'll send a small python snippet), 4) sample CSV with prompt IDs, expected label for quality checks.
[09:16] Janie Park: We'll create a small repo with the sample prompts and the driver. Expect to share by Mar 3.
[09:22] Liam O'Shea: On measurement, we'll collect: request_id, start_ts, first_byte_ts, end_ts, model_name, batch_size, tokens_generated, cache_hit, response_text, quality_score. That should let you recompute metrics.
[09:35] Janie Park: Fine. Also want to include a small human review set for outlier inspection.
[09:41] Maya Chen: Good call.
[09:43] Marcus Li: Are there any quotas or rate limits on the POC environment? If we hit the capacity and need to scale, what's the cadence?
[09:52] Liam O'Shea: For private POC we'll provision dedicated capacity sized to your expected qps and include a buffer for bursts. If you need more, we can scale GPU pools but that may change timeline slightly. We'll note autoscaling parameters in the runbook.
[10:05] Janie Park: For data residency — the POC data must remain in our EU region. Can you run the POC in eu-west-1?
[10:12] Maya Chen: Yes, we have eu-west-1 region provisioning; we'll request that for this POC.
[10:18] Liam O'Shea: A few notes about streaming measurement: first-byte is critical for perceived latency, but quality evals should always use full output. We'll instrument both and provide both charts.
[10:30] Janie Park: Agreed.
[10:32] Sofia Gomez: Anything else from the Redwood side on risks?
[10:36] Liam O'Shea: One risk is mismatch in traffic shaping; our advice is to start with a 10% shadow run using your production traffic shape to validate config before the big run.
[10:46] Janie Park: We can do that. 
[10:48] Maya Chen: Let's capture the explicit success criteria one more time: 1) p95 < 250ms for 512 token prompts, 2) sustained throughput 200 qps with burst to 450 without p95 spikes beyond 1.5x, 3) quality regression <= 2% on classification metrics, 4) cost within expected budget (we'll define budget in follow-up). Are we comfortable with that?
[11:12] Janie Park: Yes.
[11:14] Sofia Gomez: Yes.
[11:16] Marcus Li: Ok.
[11:18] Liam O'Shea: Next steps recap — we'll: 1) share harness repo + adapter example (Liam), 2) send network checklist & security pack (Maya), 3) customer to upload scripts and prompt set (Janie). We'll schedule dry runs and formal benchmark as discussed.
[11:36] Maya Chen: I'll send calendar invites for benchmark windows and a shared doc for results.
[11:42] Priya Nair: I'll track action items and follow up on due dates.
[11:46] Janie Park: One question — do you support a test where we vary quantization levels during run to assess regression?
[11:53] Liam O'Shea: Yes we can include quantization A/B and run quality checks per config. We'll note GPU memory and perf for each.
[12:01] Sofia Gomez: Great. Any blockers from Acme on the network side?
[12:05] Marcus Li: We'll need IP ranges and an ETA on the peering details so SREs can prep.
[12:11] Maya Chen: We'll share IP ranges in the harness doc today.
[12:15] Janie Park: Ok no other questions.
[12:18] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[12:22] Liam O'Shea: Thanks, bye.
---
End of transcript.
